title: Alwar Travel Guide: History, Attractions & Things to Do
content:
Alwar

Alwar, located in the royal state of Rajasthan, is a lesser-known yet stunning destination rich in heritage, culture, and natural beauty. Surrounded by the scenic Aravalli Hills, Alwar offers the perfect blend of historic forts, serene lakes, ancient temples, and wildlife sanctuaries. Its close proximity to both Delhi (160 km) and Jaipur (150 km) makes it a popular weekend getaway for travelers looking to explore Rajasthan beyond the usual tourist trail.

The history of Alwar dates back thousands of years. Once part of the ancient Matsya Kingdom, the region has seen the rise and fall of many rulers including the Rajputs, Mughals, and later the British. Alwar was officially founded in 1770 by Pratap Singh, a Rajput ruler, and has since been known for its strong cultural roots, stunning palaces, and heroic past.

Top attractions include the majestic Bala Quila (Alwar Fort), the stunning City Palace, and the Sariska Tiger Reserve, known for its tigers, leopards, and safaris. For peaceful escapes, head to Siliserh Lake or the ancient Neelkanth Mahadev Temple in the Sariska hills. Don't miss the artistic Moosi Maharani Ki Chhatri, known for its intricate carvings.

Alwar is also a great spot for shopping-famous for traditional Rajasthani handicrafts, jewelry, and the popular sweet, Alwar ka Kalakand. Street food like kachoris and Rajasthani thalis adds to the local flavor.

The best time to visit Alwar is from October to March, when the weather is cool and pleasant. Summers (April-June) can be quite hot, while the monsoon months (July-September) offer lush greenery, especially around Sariska and the lake areas.

Major festivals like Navratri, Diwali, Dussehra, and the Alwar Festival bring the city to life with cultural performances, music, and vibrant traditions.

How to Reach Alwar

  • By Road: Well connected via NH-8 from Delhi and Jaipur.
  • By Train: Alwar Junction is connected to major cities.
  • By Air: Nearest airport is in Jaipur (approx. 150 km away).

Top Places to visit in Alwar

1.Bhangarh Fort, Rajasthan

 

The Bhangarh Fort, located in the Alwar district of Rajasthan, is one of India’s most famous and mysterious forts, often associated with legends of being haunted. Built in the 16th century by Raja Bhagwant Das for his son, Madho Singh, the fort is surrounded by the Aravalli Hills and lush greenery, making it a fascinating blend of history, architecture, and mystery.

The fort complex includes temples, palaces, and gateways, each showcasing Rajput-style architecture. Despite being in ruins, the fort’s massive walls, intricate carvings, and the serene natural surroundings attract history buffs, photographers, and curious travelers from across the world.

Bhangarh is widely known for its haunting tales and supernatural stories, which add to its allure. In fact, the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) has put up a board prohibiting entry into the fort after sunset and before sunrise, making the site even more intriguing.

  • Timings: Daily: 6:00 AM - 6:00 PM (Entry not allowed after sunset)
  • Entry Fee: Indians: ₹25 per person, Foreigners: ₹200 per person and Camera Fee: Additional charges apply

 

2. Bala Quila Fort, Alwar

 

The Bala Quila Fort, also known as the Alwar Fort, is a majestic hilltop fortress overlooking the city of Alwar in Rajasthan. Built in the 15th century by Hasan Khan Mewati, this massive fort spreads across 5 km and stands as a symbol of Rajasthan’s rich history and architectural brilliance.

Perched high on the Aravalli Hills, the fort offers panoramic views of Alwar city and its surrounding landscapes. The structure is fortified with six grand gates – Jai Pol, Suraj Pol, Laxman Pol, Chand Pol, Krishan Pol, and Andheri Gate - each reflecting the strength and grandeur of Rajput defense architecture. Inside the fort, visitors can explore palaces, temples, and stepwells, which showcase a blend of Mughal and Rajput styles.

Historically, the Bala Quila Fort has been ruled by the Mughals, Marathas, and Rajputs, making it a site of great cultural and strategic importance. Today, it is a popular destination for history enthusiasts, photographers, and travelers seeking a glimpse into Rajasthan’s royal past.

  • Timings: Daily: 10:00 AM - 5:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Indians: ₹50 per person, Foreigners: ₹200 per person and Camera Fee: ₹50

 

3. Sariska Wildlife Sanctuary, Alwar

 

The Sariska Wildlife Sanctuary, located in the Alwar district of Rajasthan, is a popular wildlife destination known for its rich biodiversity and scenic landscapes. Spread over 800 sq. km and nestled in the Aravalli Hills, it is home to the famous Bengal tigers along with leopards, striped hyenas, jackals, jungle cats, and various species of deer like sambhar and chital.

Originally the hunting grounds of the Alwar royals, Sariska was declared a wildlife reserve in 1955 and later became part of Project Tiger in 1978. Apart from its wildlife, the sanctuary is dotted with historical sites, including the Kankwari Fort, ancient temples, and medieval pavilions, blending natural beauty with cultural heritage.

The sanctuary is also a paradise for birdwatchers, with species like peafowl, sand grouse, tree pies, and eagles often spotted here. Its diverse terrain of dry deciduous forests, rocky hills, and grasslands makes it an exciting destination for safari adventures and photography. Read More…

Timings:

  • Winter (October - March): 6:30 AM - 10:30 AM, 2:00 PM - 6:00 PM
  • Summer (April - June): 6:00 AM - 10:00 AM, 2:30 PM - 6:30 PM
  • Closed during the monsoon season (July - September)

Entry Fee:

  • Indians: ₹80 per person
  • Foreigners: ₹470 per person
  • Jeep Safari: Around ₹2,500 - ₹4,000 per jeep (6 people max)
  • Canter Safari: Around ₹500 - ₹800 per person

A visit to Sariska Wildlife Sanctuary offers the perfect blend of adventure, nature, and history, making it a must-visit destination for wildlife lovers and travelers exploring Rajasthan. 

 

4. Siliserh Lake Palace, Alwar

 

The Siliserh Lake Palace is one of the most enchanting attractions in Alwar, Rajasthan. Built in 1845 by Maharaja Vinay Singh for his queen, Shila, this stunning palace sits on the banks of the picturesque Siliserh Lake, surrounded by the serene Aravalli Hills. Originally constructed as a royal hunting lodge and summer retreat, the palace today has been converted into a heritage hotel managed by RTDC (Rajasthan Tourism Development Corporation)

The palace offers a unique blend of Rajasthani architecture, scenic beauty, and historical charm. Visitors can enjoy boating in Siliserh Lake, spot migratory birds, and take in the breathtaking views of the surrounding hills. Its peaceful ambiance makes it a perfect getaway for couples, families, and history lovers alike.

Many travelers also combine their visit to Siliserh Lake Palace with nearby attractions such as the Bala Quila Fort and the Sariska Wildlife Sanctuary, making it an ideal stop on an Alwar trip.

Timings: Daily: 8:00 AM - 6:00 PM

Entry Fee: Palace/Hotel Visit: Free (charges apply for accommodation and dining)

Boating: ₹200 - ₹500 per person (depending on boat type)

A visit to the Siliserh Lake Palace, Alwar offers the perfect mix of history, luxury, and natural beauty, making it one of the most romantic and serene destinations in Rajasthan.

 

5. Hill Fort Kesroli, Alwar

 

The Hill Fort Kesroli, located about 12 km from Alwar in Rajasthan, is a 14th-century heritage fort perched dramatically on the Aravalli Hills. Built by the Yaduvanshi Rajputs, this fort has witnessed centuries of history, including rule by the Mughals, Jats, and eventually the princely state of Alwar. Today, it has been beautifully restored and converted into a heritage hotel managed by Neemrana Hotels, offering visitors a rare opportunity to stay inside a medieval fort.

The fort’s turrets, ramparts, and massive walls provide stunning panoramic views of the surrounding countryside, making it a favorite among history lovers, photographers, and couples seeking a royal getaway. The interiors of the fort are designed in traditional Rajasthani style with modern comforts, giving guests a perfect blend of heritage and luxury.

Visitors can enjoy sunset views, heritage walks, swimming, and Rajasthani cuisine while staying at the fort. Its tranquil ambiance and historical aura make it an ideal weekend retreat near Delhi and Jaipur.

Timings:

  • Day Visit: 9:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Overnight Stay: Check-in - 2:00 PM | Check-out - 12:00 Noon

Entry Fee:

  • Day Visit (with Lunch/High Tea): ₹1,000 - ₹1,500 per person (approx.)
  • Stay Packages: Starting from ₹6,000 onwards (depending on room type and season)

 

6. Neelkanth Mahadev Temple, Alwar

 

The Neelkanth Mahadev Temple, located near the Sariska National Park in Alwar district, is an ancient shrine dedicated to Lord Shiva. Built between the 6th and 9th centuries by the Pratihar rulers, the temple is renowned for its magnificent architecture and intricate stone carvings that showcase the brilliance of early medieval craftsmanship in Rajasthan.

Surrounded by the Aravalli Hills, the temple complex houses the main shrine of Lord Shiva along with several smaller temples dedicated to various deities. The highlight of the temple is its beautifully sculpted pillars, walls, and the impressive Shiva Lingam, which attracts devotees and history lovers alike.

Though partially in ruins, the temple remains a sacred site and a major attraction for pilgrims, historians, and travelers. Its serene location near Sariska also makes it a peaceful spiritual stop during wildlife or heritage tours.

  • Timings: Daily: 6:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Free (No entry fee; donations are welcome)

A visit to the Neelkanth Mahadev Temple offers a perfect combination of spirituality, history, and architectural beauty, making it one of the must-visit temples in Alwar.

 

7. Sariska Palace, Alwar

 

The Sariska Palace, located on the edge of the Sariska Tiger Reserve in Alwar, is a magnificent heritage palace that reflects the grandeur of Rajasthan’s royal past. Built in 1892 by Maharaja Jai Singh of Alwar as a hunting lodge and retreat, the palace showcases a stunning blend of French and Rajasthani architecture.

Surrounded by lush greenery and the wildlife-rich landscapes of Sariska, the palace features ornate interiors, sprawling courtyards, and regal furnishings that transport visitors back to the era of Rajasthan’s maharajas. Today, the Sariska Palace has been converted into a luxury heritage hotel, offering modern comforts while preserving its royal charm.

Guests can enjoy a unique stay experience with activities like jungle safaris, nature walks, and royal dining. Even for day visitors, the palace’s architecture, grandeur, and scenic setting make it a must-visit attraction near Sariska National Park.

Timings:

  • Day Visit: 10:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Hotel Stay: Check-in - 2:00 PM | Check-out - 12:00 Noon

Entry Fee:

  • Day Visit (Heritage Tour / Dining): ₹500 - ₹1,000 per person (approx.)
  • Stay Packages: Starting from ₹7,000 onwards (depending on room type and season)

 

8. City Palace, Alwar

 

The City Palace of Alwar, also known as the Vinay Vilas Mahal, is one of the finest architectural landmarks of Rajasthan, located at the foot of the Aravalli Hills. Built in 1793 by Raja Bakhtawar Singh, this grand palace beautifully blends Mughal and Rajput architectural styles, showcasing the opulence of the Alwar rulers.

The palace complex features massive gates, marble pavilions, grand courtyards, and intricately designed halls. The highlight is the Durbar Hall, adorned with crystal chandeliers and exquisite decorations, which once hosted royal gatherings and ceremonies. The palace also houses a museum that displays rare manuscripts, miniature paintings, royal costumes, weapons, and artifacts, giving visitors a glimpse into Alwar’s regal history.

Set against the backdrop of hills and surrounded by lush gardens, the City Palace is a favorite destination for history lovers, photographers, and travelers seeking to explore Rajasthan’s royal heritage.

  • Timings: Daily: 10:00 AM - 5:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Indians: ₹20 per person, Foreigners: ₹100 per person & Camera Fee: ₹50

 

9. Vijay Mandir Palace, Alwar

 

The Vijay Mandir Palace, located about 10 km from Alwar, is a stunning architectural marvel built by Maharaja Jai Singh Prabhakar in the early 20th century. This grand palace, overlooking the beautiful Vijay Sagar Lake, is a fine example of Rajasthan’s royal heritage and architectural elegance.

The palace features 105 ornate rooms, decorated with intricate designs, arched windows, and elegant balconies that reflect the royal grandeur of the Alwar rulers. Surrounded by lush gardens and the serene lake, the Vijay Mandir Palace offers breathtaking views and a tranquil atmosphere.

Within the palace complex lies the Sita Ram Temple, a sacred shrine that attracts devotees, especially during Ram Navami celebrations. While entry to the main palace interiors is restricted, visitors can admire its magnificent architecture and enjoy the picturesque surroundings from the outside.

  • Timings: Daily: 9:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Free (No entry fee; only special permission required to access certain palace areas)

 

10. Moosi Maharani Ki Chhatri, Alwar

 

The Moosi Maharani Ki Chhatri is a stunning red sandstone and marble cenotaph located near the City Palace of Alwar. Built in 1815 by Maharaja Vinay Singh, it was dedicated to Maharaja Bakhtawar Singh and his queen, Rani Moosi, who performed sati on his funeral pyre.

The cenotaph is a remarkable example of Rajasthani architecture, featuring intricately carved arches, domes, and floral motifs. The lower section of the structure is built in red sandstone, while the upper portion is made of white marble, symbolizing strength and purity. Inside, beautifully painted ceilings with mythological themes add to its artistic charm.

Situated in a peaceful garden near the Siliserh Lake and the City Palace, this historic monument is not only an architectural delight but also a place of cultural and historical significance. It attracts tourists, history lovers, and photographers for its serene setting and royal legacy.

  • Timings: Daily: 9:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Indians: ₹10 per person and Foreigners: ₹50 per person

 

11. The Palace Museum, Alwar

 

The Palace Museum, located inside the City Palace of Alwar, is a treasure trove of Rajasthan’s royal heritage. Established in 1940, the museum showcases an impressive collection of artifacts, including ancient manuscripts, paintings, sculptures, rare coins, and royal weaponry. One of its highlights is the grand miniature painting gallery, featuring exquisite Mughal and Rajput artworks. Visitors can also see royal costumes, musical instruments, and personal belongings of the Alwar rulers, offering a glimpse into their opulent lifestyle. The museum is divided into several sections, each preserving a unique aspect of history and culture, making it a must-visit for history and art lovers.

  • Timings: 10:00 AM - 5:00 PM
  • Closed on: Fridays and public holidays
  • Entry Fee: Indians: ₹20, Foreigners: ₹100 and Camera fee (if applicable): Extra charges may apply

 

12. Company Bagh (Purjan Vihar), Alwar

 

The Company Bagh, also known as Purjan Vihar, is a historic garden in Alwar built in 1868 during the reign of Maharaja Shiv Dan Singh. Later, Maharaja Mangal Singh added the beautiful structure called Shimla House, which provided a cool retreat during the hot summer months.

The garden is well laid out with lush lawns, flowering plants, and shaded pathways, making it an ideal place for leisurely walks and relaxation. The peaceful ambiance and colonial-era charm attract both tourists and locals, offering a refreshing escape from the bustling city.

Its central location also makes it a convenient spot to combine with visits to nearby attractions such as the City Palace and Bala Quila Fort.

  • Timings: Daily: 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Indians: ₹5 & Foreigners: ₹50

 

13. Fateh Jung Gumbad, Alwar

 

The Fateh Jung Gumbad is a stunning 5-storey tomb built in the mid-17th century, blending Mughal and Rajput architectural styles. Constructed in honor of Fateh Jang, a minister in the Mughal court of Emperor Shah Jahan, the monument is admired for its grand design and detailed carvings.

Surrounded by lush gardens, the Gumbad resembles a mini version of the Taj Mahal, showcasing Mughal elegance with Rajasthani artistry. The dome, arched gateways, and intricate lattice work make it a remarkable heritage site and a photographer’s delight.

Located close to the Delhi-Alwar road, the monument is not only a historical gem but also a serene spot for visitors to explore while in the city.

  • Timings: Daily: 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Indians: ₹5 and  Foreigners: ₹50 

 

14.  Sarafa Bazar, Alwar

 

Sarafa Bazar is one of the most popular and bustling markets in Alwar, famous for its traditional Rajasthani jewelry, handicrafts, and textiles. The market’s name “Sarafa” itself means jewelry, and true to its name, it is the best place to shop for silver ornaments, gold jewelry, and precious stones crafted in authentic Rajasthani style.

Apart from jewelry, the bazar also offers a wide range of items like traditional clothes, mojris (ethnic footwear), handicrafts, and decorative souvenirs, making it a must-visit spot for tourists looking to carry a piece of Rajasthan home.

The lively streets, colorful shops, and local vendors create a vibrant atmosphere that reflects the cultural charm of Alwar. Bargaining is common here, and exploring the market also gives visitors a chance to enjoy local street food along the way.

  • Timings: Daily: 10:00 AM - 8:00 PM (Closed on Tuesdays)
  • Entry Fee: No entry fee (shopping costs as per purchase).

 

15. Biodiversity Park, Alwar

 

The Biodiversity Park in Alwar is a lush green sanctuary designed to preserve the rich flora and fauna of the region while providing a peaceful retreat for nature lovers. Spread across several acres, the park features a diverse range of trees, plants, and flowering species, representing the unique biodiversity of Rajasthan.

It is an ideal place for morning walks, jogging, photography, and family outings, offering a refreshing escape from the hustle and bustle of the city. Educational boards and guided trails in the park also help visitors learn about different plant species, their ecological importance, and conservation efforts.

The park’s tranquil environment and well-maintained pathways make it a favorite spot for tourists, students, and locals looking to connect with nature.

  • Timings: Daily: 6:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Free (No entry fee; donations are welcome)

 

16. Churi Market, Alwar

 

Churi Market is one of the most vibrant and bustling shopping destinations in Alwar, famous for its wide variety of traditional bangles, jewelry, and ethnic accessories. The market’s name “Churi” itself refers to bangles, making it a hotspot for shoppers looking for authentic Rajasthani jewelry and handicrafts.

Apart from bangles, the market also offers ethnic clothing, footwear, decorative items, and souvenirs, making it a perfect stop for tourists to experience the local culture and bring back a piece of Rajasthan. The narrow lanes, colorful storefronts, and lively crowd create a truly immersive shopping experience.

Visitors can also enjoy local street food while exploring the market, adding to the charm of this bustling bazaar. Bargaining is common, so it’s a great place to hunt for unique finds at reasonable prices.

  • Timings: Daily: 10:00 AM - 8:00 PM (Closed on Tuesdays)
  • Entry Fee: No entry fee (Shopping costs depend on purchases)

 

17. Pandu Pol, Alwar

 

Pandu Pol is one of the historic gateways of Bala Quila Fort in Alwar, showcasing the grandeur of Rajput architecture. Named after Pandu, the legendary figure from the Mahabharata, this gate is a significant part of the fort’s defense system and reflects the strategic planning and craftsmanship of the Rajputs.

The gate is adorned with ornate arches, detailed carvings, and robust wooden doors, giving visitors a glimpse into the military architecture of medieval Rajasthan. Standing at the entrance, Pandu Pol offers breathtaking views of the surrounding city and the Aravalli hills, making it a popular spot for photography and history enthusiasts.

Pandu Pol serves as a starting point for exploring the Bala Quila Fort complex, including its palaces, temples, and other gates, providing a complete experience of Alwar’s royal heritage.

  • Timings: Daily: 10:00 AM - 5:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Indians: ₹50 per person (Bala Quila Fort entry), Foreigners: ₹200 per person and Camera Fee: ₹50

 

18. Bhartrihari Temple, Alwar

 

The Bhartrihari Temple, located in Alwar district, is an ancient shrine dedicated to Bhartrihari, the legendary Sanskrit poet and philosopher, who is believed to have renounced worldly life and meditated in this region. The temple is revered for its spiritual significance and historical value, attracting both devotees and history enthusiasts.

Set amidst serene surroundings, the temple features traditional Rajasthani architecture, with intricately carved pillars, a central sanctum, and peaceful courtyards. Pilgrims visit the temple to offer prayers and seek blessings, especially during religious festivals and special occasions associated with Bhartrihari.

The temple’s tranquil location makes it a perfect stop for those exploring Alwar’s spiritual and cultural heritage, offering both a meditative atmosphere and a glimpse into ancient Indian traditions.

  • Timings: Daily: 6:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Free (Donations are welcome)

 

19. Gharbhai (Dhubhai) Waterfall, Alwar

 

The Gharbhai Waterfall, also known as Dhubhai Waterfall, is a picturesque natural attraction located near the Sariska region in Alwar district. Nestled amidst the lush Aravalli Hills, the waterfall is a perfect spot for nature lovers, photographers, and travelers seeking a peaceful retreat.

The waterfall cascades down rocky terrain into a clear pool, surrounded by greenery and serene landscapes. It is especially enchanting during the monsoon season, when the water flow is at its peak and the surrounding hills turn vibrant green. The area is ideal for picnics, trekking, and nature walks, offering a refreshing escape from city life.

Although relatively less crowded than other tourist spots, the waterfall’s natural beauty and tranquil environment make it a hidden gem in Alwar’s scenic landscape.

  • Timings: Daily: 8:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Free (No entry fee; donations or local guides optional)

 

20. Narayani Mata Temple, Alwar

 

The Narayani Mata Temple, located in the Alwar district, is a revered Hindu shrine dedicated to Goddess Narayani, a form of Durga. Situated atop a hill, the temple offers panoramic views of the surrounding landscape, making it both a spiritual and scenic destination.

The temple is known for its traditional Rajasthani architecture, featuring carved pillars, a sanctum with the deity’s idol, and peaceful courtyards for devotees. Pilgrims visit the temple throughout the year, with Navratri and other Hindu festivals attracting large crowds who come to offer prayers and participate in religious ceremonies.

The serene surroundings, coupled with the spiritual aura, make Narayani Mata Temple an ideal spot for meditation and reflection. Many visitors combine a trip here with nearby attractions like Sariska Wildlife Sanctuary and Sariska Palace, creating a full-day spiritual and cultural itinerary.

  • Timings: Daily: 6:00 AM - 7:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Free (Donations are welcome)

 

21. Naldeshwar Shrine, Alwar

 

The Naldeshwar Shrine is a revered Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, located in the Alwar district of Rajasthan. The shrine is known for its spiritual significance, ancient architecture, and tranquil surroundings, making it a peaceful destination for devotees and travelers alike.

The temple features traditional Rajasthani stone architecture, with a central sanctum housing the Shiva Lingam. The serene environment around the shrine, often surrounded by lush greenery, provides a perfect setting for meditation, prayers, and spiritual reflection. Pilgrims and tourists frequently visit the shrine, especially during Mahashivratri, to participate in religious rituals and ceremonies.

Its location in a calm and less crowded area makes Naldeshwar Shrine an ideal stop for those exploring Alwar’s spiritual heritage along with nearby temples and historical sites.

  • Timings:  Daily: 6:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Free (Donations are welcome)

 

22. Jagannath Ji Temple, Alwar

 

The Jagannath Ji Temple in Alwar is a revered Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Jagannath, an incarnation of Lord Vishnu. Known for its spiritual ambiance and vibrant rituals, the temple attracts devotees from across the region, especially during the annual Rath Yatra, when the deity is taken out in a grand procession.

The temple architecture reflects traditional Rajasthani style with beautifully carved pillars, decorative arches, and a sanctum housing the idol of Lord Jagannath along with his siblings Balabhadra and Subhadra. Devotees visit the temple to offer prayers, participate in religious ceremonies, and seek blessings for prosperity and well-being.

Located conveniently in Alwar city, the temple is easily accessible and often included in a spiritual tour of the district, along with other notable shrines like Narayani Mata Temple and Bhartrihari Temple.

  • Timings: Daily: 6:00 AM - 7:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Free (Donations are welcome)

 

23. Ajabgarh Fort, Alwar

 

Ajabgarh Fort is a historic fort located in the Alwar district, showcasing the military architecture and strategic brilliance of medieval Rajasthan. Built centuries ago, the fort served as a defensive stronghold and is perched on a hill, providing panoramic views of the surrounding landscape.

The fort features robust ramparts, arched gateways, and watchtowers, reflecting the typical Rajput architectural style. Though partially in ruins, the fort still retains its majestic charm and historical significance, making it a fascinating site for history enthusiasts and photographers.

Visitors often combine a trip to Ajabgarh Fort with nearby attractions in Alwar, including City Palace, Bala Quila, and Company Bagh, for a comprehensive heritage tour. The fort’s serene location and scenic views also make it an excellent spot for trekking and nature walks.

  • Timings: Daily: 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Indians: ₹20 per person & Foreigners: ₹100 per person
excerpt: Alwar, a historic city in Rajasthan, offers a perfect blend of royal palaces, ancient forts, scenic lakes, and rich wildlife. Explore attractions like Bala Quila, Sariska Tiger Reserve, and Siliserh Lake just a few hours from Delhi or Jaipur. Whether you're into history, nature, or food, Alwar is an underrated gem waiting to be discovered.

faqs.answer: Top places to visit in Alwar include: Bala Quila (Alwar Fort), City Palace (Vinay Vilas Mahal), Sariska Tiger Reserve, Siliserh Lake and Palace, Moosi Maharani Ki Chhatri, Neelkanth Mahadev Temple.
